title: No Verified Police Record Can Support a Pet-Theft Dispatch
excerpt: No police seizure, court verdict, or intercepted shipment is documented here. Honest campaigning needs records before naming victims, syndicates, or crimes.
body_html:
No police seizure, court verdict, or intercepted shipment is documented in the available material. That leaves stolen families, alleged syndicates, poison baits, stun guns, transport conditions, and forged quarantine papers unverified. Publishing them as fact would turn real animal suffering into an invented scene.

Records must lead

A credible pet-theft investigation needs an official case number, named agency, date, location, procedural status, and exact seizure details. Police or court records must establish whether conduct involved theft under Vietnamese law, illegal transport, administrative breaches, or another offense. No such record appears here.

Health risk still demands precision

Rabies exposure generally occurs when infected saliva enters bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. WHO guidance supports these measures.

Demand evidence. Demand reform.

Vietnamese families deserve protection from theft, unsafe transport, uninspected slaughter, and weak enforcement. SDE’s campaign demands nationwide abolition by 2030, alongside strong quarantine controls and transparent enforcement. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action—and follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.
